turns.prompt_text: In https://www.fnbames.com, where can I get my tax INT statements? It has a route to TurboTax, but I don't use that
turns.response_html:
To find your tax 1099-INT (Interest Income) statements on the First National Bank Ames website without using the TurboTax export, you can access the PDF versions directly through your online banking portal.

Where to Find the Statements

  1. Log in to your Online Banking at fnb247.com.
  2. Select the specific account you need the information for (e.g., your Savings or Money Market account).
  3. Look for a tab or link labeled "Documents" or "Online Statements."
  4. Once in the documents section, look for a "Document Type" dropdown menu.
  5. Select "Interest Form" or "Tax Form" from the list. This will allow you to view and download the statement as a PDF rather than sending it to TurboTax.

Using the Mobile App

If you prefer to use the mobile app:

  1. Tap the "More" tab at the bottom of the screen.
  2. Select "Statements."
  3. Choose the relevant account and year to view the PDF.

If You Cannot Access Your Online Account

If you have trouble logging in or navigating the portal, you can obtain your tax information through these alternatives:

  • Phone: Call the Customer Service Center at 515-232-5561. They can verify your identity and assist with document retrieval or account access issues.
  • In-Person: You can visit a local branch, such as the Main Office at 405 5th Street in Ames, to request a printed copy of your 1099-INT.

Note that if you earned less than $10 in interest for the year, the bank is generally not required to issue a 1099-INT form, though the interest earned will still be listed on your year-end December statement.

turns.prompt_text: I have logged in and selected my simple cash back account, however there is no dropdown menu in the documents section
turns.response_html:
If you are looking at the documents section specifically within your "Simple Cash Back" account and don't see a dropdown for tax forms, there are a few reasons why that might be happening and alternative places to look:

1. Check the "Tax Forms" tab on the Main Menu

Often, banks consolidate tax documents at the profile level rather than inside a specific account's statement history.

  • Instead of clicking into your specific account first, look at the main dashboard menu (usually on the left sidebar or top navigation).
  • Look for a tab labeled "Documents," "eStatements," or "Tax Forms" that is separate from your account list. This is often where consolidated 1099s are stored.

2. Verify Interest Earnings ($10 Rule)

Banks are typically only required to issue a 1099-INT if the account earned $10.00 or more in interest during the tax year.

  • Because the "Simple Cash Back" account focuses on rewards/rebates rather than interest, it may not have generated enough (or any) interest to trigger a form.
  • If you earned less than $10, the "Tax Form" option often won't appear in the menu at all. In this case, you can find your total interest earned for the year by looking at your December statement, which will have a "Year-to-Date Interest Paid" summary.

3. Check "Notices"

Sometimes tax documents are categorized under "Notices" rather than "Statements" or "Tax Forms." If you see a "Notices" folder in your documents section, check there for any PDFs issued in late January or early February.

4. Direct Assistance in Ames

Since navigating the online portal can be hit-or-miss depending on the browser version, you can get the exact status of your document by contacting the local support team:

  • Phone: Call 515-232-5561 and ask for "Online Banking Support." They can look at your specific profile and tell you if a 1099-INT was generated.
  • In-Person: If you are near the Main Office (405 5th Street) or the South Ames branch, a personal banker can print the statement for you at the desk with a photo ID.
